cases.prompt: We have two candidate dashboard layouts and no evidence which one gets users to the primary action faster. Build throwaway mockups and compare before we commit.
Unknown whether a streaming parser can hold the 10k-row page under 50ms. Spike it in a scratch benchmark before proposing the change.
We think inline editing will cut form abandonment but have no data. Run a small observable experiment to decide.
Not sure the new charting library can render 100k points at 60fps in our stack. Try it in a disposable prototype.
Drag-to-reorder versus up/down buttons: unclear which our users understand. Prototype both and watch a quick session.
It is untested whether we can consume the queue with backpressure under peak load. Build an isolated experiment to find out.
Would denormalizing the events table actually speed the monthly report? Measure it on a scratch copy before deciding.
Spike whether we can swap the parser implementation without touching any call sites, then throw the spike away.
Two-step versus three-step onboarding: no evidence which completes better. Make a throwaway prototype of each and compare.
Server-rendered or client-rendered for this page is an open question; prototype both and measure time-to-interactive.
Add a GET /health endpoint that returns 200 and the build SHA, exactly as described in the task.
Rename this helper to match the established naming convention across its three call sites.
Format this module with the repository formatter.
Fix the off-by-one in this pagination offset; the cause and expected result are already established.
Apply the known one-line version bump requested in the release checklist.
Add the already specified created_at ISO-8601 field to this DTO and its serializer.
Change the already identified staging URL from http to https in this one config value.
Run the focused unit tests for the parser module.
Review this authentication change for security issues.
Prototype the checkout against the live Stripe account with real charges to see what breaks.

quality_comparisons.objective_verifier: The deterministic fixture includes a representative UI-variant comparison and a representative falsifiable technical spike as positive prompts, and the capability instruction requires each to declare a question, options/hypotheses and bounds, run in an isolated area, and end with a recorded decision plus evidence reference.

The fixture contains ten hard-negative prompts, including a fully specified task and an experiment that would require live production credentials and real charges, and none of them trigger the capability.

The capability instruction requires temporary state to be cleaned by default, retention to be explicit and policy-compatible, and prototype code never to be promoted into production source automatically; follow-on implementation enters the ordinary managed OpenSpec lifecycle.
